Futures markets ended the week Friday much the same way as how they started it on Monday, with long liquidation a feature all week amid the USDA's loosening of balance sheets a week ago and there being little offsetting bullish input that ensued. Charts have become oversold in recent days as the selling pressed on, but we maintain that the bull camp is going to need some sort of new input to push prices back higher with the funds now coming out of their long position a bit and with US crop sizes generally known in another few weeks. The transition from US crop focus to South American crop focus will remain ongoing.<br /> <br />Corn Summary-<br />Corn futures fell to new lows for the week on Friday, taking out the bottom end of the range seen the rest of the week this week but still holding above the report day low from last Friday. Inversely, cash markets showed some strength the back half of the week, with farmers still opting to push for bean harvest where able and as rains slowed those who had finished bean harvest already the last couple days. That said though, as dryness shows back up next week, it’s expected that a sizeable chunk of the crop is going to come across the scales in the next ten days, which could lead to increased farmer hedge selling. Aside from that, it will be South American weather and the prospects for Chinese buying that remain the loudest and will have the biggest impact on price direction longer term.  <br /> <br />Soybean Summary-<br />Soybean futures made it a perfect five for five to the downside this week, scoring new lows for the move for the second straight day and closing lower on what continues to be long liquidation by the funds and hedge selling by the farmer. Chinese buying has remained steady, but traders are aware that there's a cap on this current run of purchases and are curious as to what happens with business beyond the first of the new year. Industry sources also estimate upwards of a quarter of the crop could've been harvested over the last week to 10 days, and if just half of this was sold across the scales it would more than offset the couple million tons of purchases done by the Chinese. Usage remains good and is up from a year ago, but a record crop in Brazil followed by a record crop in the US will go a long way towards satisfying that demand.<br /> <br />Wheat Summary-<br />Wheat futures led the push to the downside on Friday, scoring new lows both for the week and the larger down move on a continued lack of buying interest and as global fund traders seem to continue to be interested in using US wheat futures as the short side of hedges both against futures in Europe and also against broader length in the rest of the ag space. We talked about it earlier this week, but cash markets in the EU are just barely starting to show signs of tightening due to the ongoing situation in the Black Sea. However, tighter markets across the pond are still notably cheaper than export offers from the US, and until this changes, it’s probably difficult for the US market to see a ton of upside price movement.
